To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The presence of time-delay elements in a cluster can lead to a degradation in the performance (i.e., the mean time to failure) of a load-balanced system, and (ii) This degradation is more severe when the delays are large and uncertain.
the presence of random time delay (in addition to the deterministic delay) can lead to an increase in the queue size, and the increase is proportional to the magnitude of the random delay.

the presence of random time delays in the communication medium between the nodes of a cluster of computers can significantly affect the expected performance of a load balancing algorithm, and that the magnitude of this effect depends on the magnitude and uncertainty of the time delays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a stochastic model of the dynamic behavior of the load-balancing algorithm and its application to the design of a load-balanced cluster.
the development of a theoretical and experimental methodology to study the effects of time delay in load-balancing policies.
the analysis of the effects of time-delay uncertainty on the performance of a distributed system that employs a load-balancing strategy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of delays, deterministic or random, can significantly degrade the performance of a dynamic load-balancing policy and, therefore, the design of a load-balanced distributed system should include a careful consideration of the effect of delays.
the performance of load-balancers is significantly affected by the delays and that the magnitude of this effect depends on the magnitude of the delay, as well as the uncertainty in it.
the presence of random time delay in a distributed computing system can have a significant impact on the performance of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the performance of the load balancing algorithm in such systems should be evaluated in the presence of the various time delays, and the load balancing mechanism should be adjusted accordingly to achieve the desired performance.
the performance of a dynamic load-balancing algorithm is highly sensitive to the presence of time delays.
, in a system in which the time delays are large and random, load balancing should be performed in such a way that it is not too sensitive to the delays.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a load-balancing scheme should be designed with an appropriate level of load-transfer to compensate for the presence of time delays.
, in the design of load balancing policies in large-scale systems, it is important to consider the effect of the time delays on the system dynamics.
the performance of a distributed load-balancing policy can be significantly affected by the presence of communication delays, and that such a policy must be designed with the delays in mind.
